basis.title: CNA e-Tool Estimated Useful Life Table
basis.by: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
basis.label: Boilers, Gas Fired, Sectional
basis.note: Same life for family and elderly properties. US multifamily housing. HUD does not separate condensing from non-condensing boilers; its gas-fired sectional and atmospheric rows describe non-condensing types. Its oil/gas/dual-fuel rows (30 years low MBH, 40 years high MBH) are not used because they do not say which kind.

basis.title: CNA e-Tool Estimated Useful Life Table
basis.by: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
basis.label: Boilers, Gas Fired Atmospheric
basis.note: Same life for family and elderly properties. US multifamily housing.

basis.title: Energy Conservation Program: Energy Conservation Standards for Consumer Boilers (notice of proposed rulemaking), 88 FR 55128, August 14, 2023
basis.by: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy
basis.label: "average lifetime of consumer boilers, which is estimated to be 26.9 years for gas-fired hot water boilers"
basis.note: Printed page 55130. Consumer (residential, under 300,000 Btu/h input) gas-fired hot-water boilers, condensing and non-condensing given the same lifetime. DOE's analysis includes consumer boilers installed in commercial buildings. Also in Table IV.9 (PDF p.34, printed 55161): 'GHW: 26.9 years'.

basis.title: Updated Buildings Sector Appliance and Equipment Costs and Efficiencies (March 2023), Appendix A: EIA - Technology Forecast Updates - Residential and Commercial Building Technologies - Reference Case (Guidehouse and Leidos, March 3, 2023)
basis.by: U.S. Energy Information Administration; Appendix A prepared by Guidehouse and Leidos
basis.label: Average Life (y): 2018 installed base 25; 2022 typical (85% thermal efficiency) 25, high (99%) 25; same through 2050
basis.note: Printed page 119 (Appendix A). Commercial packaged gas-fired hot-water boiler, 800 kBtu/h input (note 1: small 300-2,500 kBtu/h hot water class). The 85% 'typical' is non-condensing and the 99% 'high' is condensing; both carry 25 years. The 2012 installed-base column shows 30 years. The data-source sheet (PDF p.231, A-51) labels the life source only under the 2012 column, as 'Comm. Heating, AC, WH EERE 2009' (a DOE analysis); the 2018-and-later life cells have no separate label.

open_questions: Every source here is a published planning, design or accounting life. None is observed replacement data.
